audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows were inverted relative to the page's own prose: level 1 was Renekton while 'early' says outright 'Level 1 is hers', levels 3 and 4-5 were Quinn while whys[2] calls level 3 'Renekton's cleanest kill window' and whys[3] says your sustain outheals her poke, and level 6 was Renekton while whys[4] says Behind Enemy Lines lets her leave on any shove.
audit.why: Renekton's window in this lane is narrow and specific — levels 3 through 5, after Slice and Dice is up and before her Ghostblade. Everything either side belongs to Quinn.
audit.corrected: Quinn, Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Quinn, Quinn, Quinn in both layers as one atomic group; ratings become 3/4/7/7/4/4/4, the inverse of the 7/6/3/3/6/6/6 already set on her side.
sources: mirrorFindings point 3 and its note naming the inverse rows

audit.why: Spikes correctly identify levels 2-3, Dominus at 6, her Youmuu's timing, and the two-item lethality wall. Behind Enemy Lines has a 3s cooldown, which is why her level-6 spike is about map presence rather than a lane cooldown you can track.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault was described as her 'self-peel' and, in the 'late' text, as knocking YOU back. Riot's text says the opposite: she dashes to you, briefly interrupts you, then leaps off and lands near her maximum attack range away. She moves, you do not. The interrupt and the 12s rank-1 cooldown were both absent, as was the fact that Behind Enemy Lines is a channel your stun cancels.
audit.why: Quinn E: 'Quinn dashes to an enemy... Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away from the target', 12s at rank 1. Quinn R carries the channel flag. Getting the direction wrong changes the chase: you do not need to walk back in from a knockback, you need to close a full attack range she just created.
audit.corrected: Vault is now stated as an interrupt that carries HER away with its 12s cooldown, and her R is named as a channel an empowered W stun cancels.
sources: kit: Quinn E text and cd
mirrorFindings point 4 ('Rewritten as Vault away, which is what actually happens')

audit.whatIsWrong: Every reference to 'Vault's cooldown' was qualitative — 'a real cooldown', 'when it's down' — with no number anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Vault at 12s rank 1 versus Slice and Dice at 16s rank 1 is the actual maths of the lane: her escape comes back before your engage does, which is why you commit only when you have seen it spent.
audit.corrected: The 12s figure is now on the page in the do's and in Key Ability Interactions.

edits.before: Her self-peel. W-stun when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Vault is 12s at rank 1 — she leaps off you and lands a screen away. Bait it.

edits.before: Track Quinn's Vault (Dash/Blind): Her self-peel. W-stun when it’s down. When it is down — W-stun + Q her.
edits.after: Vault (12s) interrupts you and carries her away, not you — and her R is a channel your W stun cancels.

edits.before: Vault (E) your W stun the moment you close the gap to reset spacing and blind your follow-up autos
edits.after: Vault off you the moment you close — it interrupts you and lands her a full attack range away

edits.before: Two items in and this lane belongs to Quinn: Ghostblade plus a Lethality second item means her Harrier burst in a single marked-auto trade hits harder than your empowered Q can heal back, and your E range can never match her passive movement speed. Stop trying to win the 1v1 and start winning the map — shove the wave, rotate for dragons and Rift Herald, and let your team composition punish the 4v5 she creates every time she roams. If forced to duel late, bait the Vault before you commit E-W or she knocks you back and kites you to death on the blind cooldown.
edits.after: Two items in and this lane belongs to Quinn: Ghostblade plus a Lethality second item means her Harrier burst in a single marked-auto trade hits harder than your empowered Q can heal back, and your E range can never match her passive movement speed. Stop trying to win the 1v1 and start winning the map — shove the wave, rotate for dragons and Rift Herald, and let your team composition punish the 4v5 she creates every time she roams. If forced to duel late, bait Vault before you commit E-W: it interrupts you and lands her a full attack range away, and it is back in 8s at rank 5.

notes: Four chart rows proposed as matched full/content pairs in one group, matching both the packet and the inverse of the already-audited Quinn side. Data discrepancy for the user: the brief header says games 590 while the packet inside says 461 for this matchup. Not asserted: whether Blinding Assault's blind affects only basic attacks or also your ability damage — Riot's text says only 'hinder its vision', so the page's existing claim that it 'shuts off your healing autos' was left as-is rather than extended into ability territory I cannot verify from the kit.
